name: g_senrekiCompletedFlagIdsA
comment: Flag-id table A for the 'senreki' (play-record) completion counter: 10 groups of 4 u16 save-progress flag ids. Save_Senreki_CountCompletedFlagsA copies it to the stack and counts a group when any of its four flag bits is set in the save flag bitmask at saveData+0x4B30.
evidence: Literal 0x005B190C in Save_Senreki_CountCompletedFlagsA (0x005B1888): std_memcpy(local_68, 0x007250BC, 0x50) then loops iVar2=0..9 and i=0..3 testing ((u32*)(saveData+0x4B30))[id>>5] bit (id&0x1F). 0x50 bytes / 2 = 40 u16 = 10 groups; first words are consecutive ids 0x09B7,0x09B8,... in rodata_00725000.s.

name: g_senrekiCompletedFlagIdsE
comment: Flag-id table E for the 'senreki' (play-record) completion counter: 12 groups of 4 u16 save-progress flag ids tested against the save flag bitmask at saveData+0x4B30.
evidence: Literal 0x005B1CF4 in Save_Senreki_CountCompletedFlagsE (0x005B1C70): std_memcpy(local_78, 0x0072514C, 0x60), group loop 0..0xB (12 groups) of 4 ids, same bitmask test as the A/B/C/D siblings. 0x60 bytes = 48 u16; initial word 0x06CE06CD gives the first ids 0x06CD,0x06CE.

name: g_saveMemberPresenceOffsets
comment: Seven {u16 partySlot, u16 presentByteOffset} pairs telling the save loader which party slots have a stored character record: for slots 1..6 the loader tests the byte at save block (work+0x24A98) + 0x2A70 + offset (0x145,0x146,0x147,0x149,0x14A,0x14B); slot 0 is special-cased (pair {0,0xFFFF}) and always applied.
evidence: Literal 0x0064D118 in maybe_Save_ApplyRecordToWork (0x0064CB24): `*(char*)((int)piVar13 + *(u16*)(0x007288C8 + uVar16*4 + 2) + 0x2A70) != 0` for uVar16=1..6, with piVar13 = work+0x24A98; uVar16==0 forces bVar17=true. Raw rodata pairs read {0,0xFFFF},{1,0x145},{2,0x146},{3,0x147},{4,0x149},{5,0x14A},{6,0x14B}.

name: g_saveDataLimits
comment: Save-data limit/descriptor record: word 0 = 9,999,999 (gold/value clamp), +0x04 = 99 (level cap), +0x08 = 255 (byte/count cap), +0x0C = default 4-byte-entry init function 0x00611FF4 (writes 0xFFFF/0), +0x10 = dispatch flags (0). Ui_DataPanel_WriteItemInfoToBuffer clamps a value against word 0, and maybe_Save_BuildSectionList dispatches through +0xC/+0x10.
evidence: Literals 0x00115928 (maybe_Save_BuildSectionList 0x001153B4: ldr pcVar at +0xC, flags at +0x10 then blx per section slot), 0x00611FF0 (function 0x00611FA8, same dispatch) and 0x00613320 (inside Ui_DataPanel_WriteItemInfoToBuffer 0x00613090: ldr r4,[base] = 0x0098967F, clamp cmp/movhs). Raw rodata: 0x0098967F, 0x63, 0xFF, 0x00611FF4, 0.

name: g_saveDataMountName
comment: Inline mount/device name 'data:' at the head of the save-data archive descriptor; six 8-byte path-formatter method slots follow at +0x08..+0x37 (system / Data%d / mini_%d, repeated twice). Passed to Fs_UnmountByName and Svc_ContentObject_GetSharedHandle as the mount name and used as the '%s' root when building save-file paths.
evidence: Bytes 0x0072D780..0x0072D787 = 'data:\0\0\0' (rodata dump word 0x61746164, then 0x3A, then zeros). Literal 0x002CC824 in Fs_FormatDataPath (0x002CC800) passes this address as the %s argument of '%s/Data%d'; 0x002CD018 in Save_WriteSlotStrings (0x002CCC50) reads handler slots at +0x28/+0x2C; maybe_Save_MigrateVerify calls Fs_UnmountByName(0x0072D780) and Svc_ContentObject_GetSharedHandle(0x0072D780).

name: g_saveArchiveSystemPathMethod
comment: One 8-byte ARM pointer-to-member-function slot {formatter 0x002CE46C, this-adjust 0} inside the save-archive descriptor's formatter table (entry 4 of 6, +0x20). The target tail-calls the vsnprintf wrapper with format '%s/system' and root 'data:', producing the archive's system file path.
evidence: Literal 0x002CDB4C in maybe_Save_LoadSlotHeader (0x002CD948): pcVar5 = (code*)*g_002cdb4c; uVar7 = g_002cdb4c[1]; piVar2 = save + (uVar7>>1); if (uVar7&1) thunk-adjust; (*pcVar5)(piVar2, buf, 0x105, param_2). Raw bytes at 0x002CE46C: mov ip,r2; mov r0,r1; ldr r3,=0x0072D780; add r2,pc,#8 -> '%s/system'; b 0x0051BA9C (vsnprintf wrapper).

name: g_saveArchiveMiniPathMethod
comment: One 8-byte ARM pointer-to-member-function slot {Fs_FormatMiniPath 0x002CE660, this-adjust 0} inside the save-archive descriptor's formatter table (entry 6 of 6, +0x30). It builds the archive's 'mini' slot-record path '%s/mini_%d' and is used for the second save string block and for loading slot records.
evidence: Literal 0x002CD028 in Save_WriteSlotStrings (0x002CCC50) and maybe_Save_WriteSlotRecords (0x002CC834): pcVar5 = (code*)*g_002cd028; uVar7 = g_002cd028[1]; (*pcVar5)(save + (uVar7>>1), buf, 0x105, slot). 0x002CE660 = Fs_FormatMiniPath, whose body passes '%s/mini_%d' and root 0x0072D780 to 0x0051BA9C.

name: g_saveCryptoBlowfishInitP
comment: Default Blowfish P-array (18 subkeys) for the save-data cipher: Save_Crypto_ExpandKey copies it (0x48 bytes) to the stack, XORs the user key into it, then runs the nine encrypt rounds that rebuild the schedule. Initial word 0x243F6A88 is the first hex digit of pi, the standard Blowfish P[0].
evidence: Literal 0x005F1030 in Save_Crypto_ExpandKey (0x005F0E64): std_memcpy(local_98, 0x0072D8F4, 0x48) then `while (i < 0x12)` (18 words) XORs key bytes into it. 0x48 bytes = 18 u32; initial 0x243F6A88 = Blowfish P[0].

name: g_saveCryptoBlowfishInitS
comment: Default Blowfish S-boxes for the save-data cipher: four boxes of 256 u32 subkeys copied by Save_Crypto_ExpandKey (0x1000 bytes) and then re-keyed with the running encrypted block, 256 words per box. Initial word 0xD1310BA6 is the standard Blowfish S0[0].
evidence: Literal 0x005F1034 in Save_Crypto_ExpandKey (0x005F0E64): std_memcpy(auStack_1098, 0x0072D93C, 0x1000), then `while (i < 4)` copies each 0x400-byte box to ctx+0x48+i*0x400 and rekeys `iVar7 < 0x100` words. 0x1000 bytes = 1024 u32 = 4 x 256; initial 0xD1310BA6 = Blowfish S0[0].

name: g_saveCryptoCrc16Table
comment: 256-entry CRC-16 lookup table for the save-data integrity check: Save_Crypto_Context_Init copies the 512 bytes to ctx+0x1058 and the MAC helper 0x005F07A4 indexes it as u16[256]. First entries are 0x0000 and 0xC0C1, the reflected CRC-16/IBM (ARC) table; SealBlock/OpenBlock compare the inverted 16-bit result over 11 bytes.
evidence: Literal 0x005F0864 in maybe_Save_CopyChecksumTable (0x005F082C) copies 0x200 bytes; caller Save_Crypto_Context_Init (0x005F0E14) stores it at ctx+0x1058. Disassembly of 0x005F07A4: ldrh r3,[r0 + (byte^0xFF)*2]; eor r3,#0xFF ... mvn r0,r3; uxth r0,r0 -> reflected CRC-16 over r2 bytes. Table words start 0xC0C10000 = u16 0x0000,0xC0C1.

name: g_fieldObject2DSharedVtable
comment: Shared base vtable for the 2-D field-object class: Field_Object2D_CtorA runs the actor base constructor and installs this table before the concrete factory vtable (0x77xxxx) replaces it. Slots are 0x002658FC (complete destructor), 0x002658D0, 0x001FEFC0 and 0x001F96D4.
evidence: Literal 0x002658CC in Field_Object2D_CtorA (0x00265878, the function the batch still calls maybe_Save_CreateSlot): *result = 0x0075CCA0 after Actor_BaseObject_Ctor; structs.json maps 0x0075CCA0 to a 4-slot vtable; R_026 evidence says the three callers are the 2-D field-object factories (Kind35/Kind36/Type1362) which overwrite it with their own 0x77xxxx table.

name: g_saveSlotPanelVtable
comment: Vtable of the save-slot UI panel object built by maybe_Save_SlotUi_Ctor: word 0 is the complete destructor 0x0045E700, words 1-5 are null, and the Ui widget interface at +0x18 holds Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchUpdate (0x001A5EE0), Ui_Widget_DispatchActiveChildren (0x001A5DC0), Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchUpdate (0x001A5D4C), Ui_MessagePage_Update (0x004A6810) and 0x001DAA20.
evidence: Literal 0x0045E6FC in maybe_Save_SlotUi_Ctor (0x0045E6A0): *self = 0x00780B20 on entry and again after maybe_Task_ThreadEntry; the ctor initialises three intrusive-list sentinels. structs.json maps the code part at 0x00780B38 as 5 slots and the next table at 0x00780B54, so this block is 11 words; methods read from rodata_00765000.s.

name: maybe_g_fsArchiveEntryEmptyTemplate
comment: Static 16-byte template used to initialise stack Fs archive/file objects: word 0 and word 3 are the vtable 0x00780D60 (which carries Fs_ArchiveEntry_Seek at +0xC and Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadAt at +0x20), words 1-2 are the secondary interface pointer 0x0072D7E8. Functions copy it into a local before Fs_SplitResourceName / Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadInto.
evidence: Literals 0x002CD020 and 0x002CDB54 (Save_WriteSlotStrings / maybe_Save_LoadSlotHeader) load 0x00780D20 into a stack object: ldr r0,[pc] -> 0x00780D20; ldr r2,[r0] -> 0x00780D60; ldr r2,[r2,#-0x30] (vbase offset 0) and ldr r0,[r0,#0xC] -> 0x00780D60, then Fs_SplitResourceName(local+1,...). Raw rodata: 0x00780D60,0x0072D7E8,0x0072D7E8,0x00780D60; vtable 0x00780D60 words include 0x00503FEC (Fs_ArchiveEntry_Seek) and 0x00503FC0 (Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadAt).

name: maybe_g_rodata_780F84
comment: Zero-initialised 4-byte rodata word loaded by the GPU-channel/Save_AsyncReadWorker thread (0x001170CC) and stored into the thread's local request structure at [sp+4] just before the 6-byte record copy; no reader or writer resolves its meaning, so the name is deliberately left as an address placeholder.
evidence: Only literal 0x0011797C in Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC): ldr r5,[pc,#0x824] at 0x00117150 yields 0x00780F84 and 0x001173A0 does str r5,[sp,#4] before bl 0x0011FFD8 (copy of 6 bytes from the read buffer to the request). 0x00780F84..0x00780F88 are zero in rodata_00765000.s; no other literal references it.

name: g_saveCryptoContextVtable
comment: Vtable of the save-data crypt context: installed at *ctx by Save_CryptoContext_Destroy. Seven words: complete destructor 0x005EF028, two header words (0), deleting destructor 0x005EF00C, shared stubs 0x00669AE0 / 0x00669AE8, and 0x005EF328. It has exactly the same layout as the neighbouring MoLive filter vtables at 0x00784294.
evidence: Literal 0x005EF324 in Save_CryptoContext_Destroy (0x005EF028): `*ctx = 0x007842B8` (ctx is the outer context initialised by Save_Crypto_Context_Init 0x005F0E14). Raw rodata 0x007842B8..0x007842D4 = 0x005EF028, 0, 0, 0x005EF00C, 0x00669AE0, 0x00669AE8, 0x005EF328; structs.json maps the code part 0x007842C4 as 4 slots and the next table starts at 0x007842DC.

name: maybe_g_saveValidateItemRecords
comment: Retail-disabled validation switch in the save-record loader: when non-zero, maybe_Save_ApplyRecordToWork walks the record's stored item-id lists and calls Item_LookupRecord for every id; in the retail image the byte is 0 and the lookups are skipped.
evidence: Only literal 0x0064D11C in maybe_Save_ApplyRecordToWork (0x0064CB24): `if (*0x007A7114 != '\0') { ... for (...) Item_LookupRecord(auStack_38,*(u16*)((int)table+2)); ... }` in both the party-record and the fallback branch. Data word is zero in the retail image.

name: g_gpuChannelStatusByte2
comment: Third byte of the GPU-channel work/status word at 0x007B0080: Gfx_OpenGpuChannel clears it when starting the channel, and the channel worker thread (0x001170CC) stores a decoded record byte there after a successful read. Part of the same little-endian u32 that G_022 named g_gpuChannelStatus.
evidence: Literal 0x001179A0 in Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC): `*0x007B0082 = bStack_bb;` after local_c0==0x10 record decode; Gfx_OpenGpuChannel (0x0010BB34) does `strb r8,[r6,#2]` with r6=0x007B0080 and also clears work+3/+5. The neighbouring global 0x007B0080 is named g_gpuChannelStatus in G_022.

name: g_gpuChannelIpcCommandBuffer
comment: Three-byte IPC command buffer at GPU-channel work+6: Gfx_OpenGpuChannel copies the channel configuration bytes (0x100 / device bytes) into it, and the channel worker sends the three bytes with func_001228A8(&g_gpuChannelIpcCommandBuffer, 3) (Os_IpcSendCommand0D/0E).
evidence: Literal 0x00117980 in Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC): uVar1 = 0x007B0086; uVar4 = func_001228A8(uVar1, 3). Gfx_OpenGpuChannel (0x0010BB34): func_00116A14(0x007B0080+6, &local_44, 3) right after maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel. func_001228A8 (0x001228A8) dispatches to Os_IpcSendCommand0D (0x00123D68) / Os_IpcSendCommand0E (0x00123C54) and returns the IPC result.

name: g_gpuChannelTimeoutRemaining
comment: Fraction of the GPU-channel wait timeout still remaining: initialised to 1.0f, recomputed by maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline as 1.0 - elapsed/total from the system tick and clamped at 0. The worker at 0x001170CC passes its address as the 'now' value while polling for the channel response.
evidence: Literal 0x00117988 in Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC): maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline(0x007B0090, &local_58, &local_70, local_64). maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline (0x0011DF50) ends with `*now = 0x3F800000 - fVar13 / ((float)uVar14 / (float)request); *now = max(*now, 0)`. Raw data word at 0x007B0090 = 0x3F800000 = 1.0f.
